1830.s: But he wint to church the first Sunday he was here, and, as Prodestants is scarce, he was welkim to the parson; and so that he mightn't disgrace the congregation, the parson gev him some dacent clothes: and thin he got him to do odd jobs for him, one way or another; and so he made himself plazin' somehow to the parson, and got on one step afther another.

1830.s: And then, your worship, I'd no clothes that was dacent to go out in, and to go to jontlemen's houses with such tatters as these, Mr. Wheelwright, says I, it would not do by any manner of means, says I.

1850.s: I had heard your name, sir, and I thought I would find you out; and if you want a lad, I will work for you for my kape, and a few dacent clothes."
1850.au: Roughing it in the bush; | or, Life in Canada ...

1850.s: …O'donahue did his best, if not for his employer, at least for himself, it was with some difficulty that he contrived to support, with anything like respectability (which in that part of the country means "dacent clothes to wear "), a very numerous family, lineally descended from the most ancient of all the kings of Ireland.

My mother brought the doctor to see him, and by selling all our dacent clothes, she got for him whatever was wanting, but all to no use: 'twas the will of the Lord to take him to himself, and he died after a few day's illness.
1850.au: Home made happy, or, Pictures of every-day life for the family circle.

1860.s: Bud here's a dacent coat; — the old caubeen* isn't very bad, because it's my Sunday one, an' not the old one of all, and isn't wid me more nor a year; an' my old brogues is bran new; not six months agone since they war in the brogue maker…

1870.s: Tie him tight, Riddle; there, another double; there now, that's as dacent a tied pair IV heels as iver lay over boord at a wake.

1870.s: Yes, yer honour, I'll come; but I've no clothes respectable and dacent; will ye put up wid the same garments if they be clane washed, yer honour?" ''

Yes, yer honour, I'll come; but I've no clothes respectable and dacent; will ye put up wid the same garments if they be clane washed, yer honour 1" "Oh yes," answered the gentleman; "as long as your hands and face are quite clean, and your clothes clean, that will…
